To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) hierarchical generative models do not learn hierarchical features when trained using some existing variational approaches; (ii) the hierarchical features learned by these models are limited to the features that can be learned by a single-layer generative model; (iii) a new variational approach can be used to train generative models with multiple layers that learn hierarchical features.
We prove that existing variational inference methods cannot take advantage of a hierarchical latent variable model when training a generative model.
